question: Which of the following Union Ministries introduced The Bills of Lading Bill, 2024 in August 2024 in the Lok Sabha?

options.text: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bills of Lading Bill, 2024, was introduced by the **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways** in August 2024 in the Lok Sabha.
 
• The bill aims to replace the existing legislative framework governing **bills of lading**, which are key documents in maritime trade.
 
• It seeks to modernize and streamline the process of issuing and managing bills of lading in line with **international best practices**.
 
• This legislative update is expected to **enhance transparency, reduce fraud, and improve efficiency** in India’s shipping and trade sector.
 
• The bill is part of India’s broader efforts to strengthen its **maritime and logistics infrastructure** to support its growing economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bill of Lading:**

 
 
• A bill of lading is a legal document issued by a carrier to acknowledge receipt of cargo for shipment.
 
• It serves as a shipment receipt, a document of title, and a contract between the shipper and the carrier.
 
• Digitalization of bills of lading is a growing trend globally to improve efficiency in maritime trade.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways:**
 
 
• This ministry is responsible for formulating and implementing policies related to shipping, ports, and waterways in India.
 
• It oversees major ports, inland waterways, and maritime trade regulations.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the development of India’s maritime infrastructure to boost economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Maritime Trade in India:**
 
 
• India has a coastline of over 7,500 km and relies heavily on maritime trade for its economic activities.
 
• Approximately 95% of India’s trade by volume and 70% by value is conducted through maritime routes.
 
• Modernizing laws and infrastructure is essential to support India’s role in global trade.
 
 
 
• **International Maritime Organization (IMO):**
 
 
• The IMO is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for regulating shipping.
 
• It promotes safe, secure, and efficient shipping on clean oceans.
 
• India’s new bill aligns with IMO standards to improve global interoperability in maritime trade.
